question:
Which of the following statements are correct?
1. The player used Forbidden Word Technique while fighting Non-Able (不能).
2. The player used Immobilize (定身术) while fighting Mad Tiger (疯虎).
3. The player used A Pluck of Many (身外身法) while fighting the Insect General.
4. The player used Cloud Step (聚形散气) while fighting Red Boy (红孩儿).

db_evidence.notes: Statement 2's clue window (20460-20601) is reliably retrieved by semantic_search on 'immobilize/定身术/Mad Tiger' in every rollout and clip_qa correctly confirms it in 4/5 rollouts. Statement 1's clue window (38151-38336) is retrievable but is adjacent to a decoy 'skill unlock' text hit at 37860-37890 (event_steps: 'glowing hexagonal skill emblem labeled 禁字法... 禁字法，不杀敌，只克己') that pulled every rollout except rollout-4 into probing 33300-39270, all outside the true window; only rollout-4 widened its window enough to overlap 38151-38336 and got it right. Statement 3's clue window (56816-56942) was never queried by any of the 5 rollouts; episodes text there describes 'a large, pale, armored monster... bulbous head and long limbs' without an obvious insect label, and the entities table instead surfaces multiple decoy insect-boss entries at other times (50670, 51360, 73080, 80400, 83250-84180), none of which is the true clue interval -- this looks like a genuine DB entity-labeling/retrievability gap rather than purely an agent search failure. Statement 4's clue window (75466-75603) is well covered by episodes/event_steps text, none of which mentions 聚形散气 or any cloud/mist skill name -- only generic flame/spark/tendril combat -- yet clip_qa hallucinated a 聚形散气 activation in 4 of 5 rollouts, suggesting the visual sub-agent over-interprets ordinary explosion/smoke VFX as the named skill.

root_causes: Statement 1: semantic_search/run_sql repeatedly anchored on a nearby 'skill unlock' popup text hit (37860-37890) instead of the actual in-combat usage window (38151-38336), causing 4/5 rollouts to probe the wrong time and wrongly reject statement 1.

Statement 3: the boss actually fought in the true clue window (56816-56942) is not tagged as an 'insect' entity in the memory DB, while several other, wrong-time insect-boss entities are prominently tagged and returned by semantic_search/entity lookups; no rollout ever queried the true window, so statement 3 was effectively unanswerable from the tools used.

Statement 4: the clip_qa visual sub-agent hallucinated a specific-named skill activation (聚形散气) from generic combat VFX (mist, transparency, sparks) in 4/5 rollouts, contradicting both the reference answer and the textual episodes/event_steps descriptions of the same interval, which mention no such skill.
Statement 2 was reliably retrieved and correctly confirmed in 4/5 rollouts; rollout-3's single failure here is an isolated visual misread rather than a systematic retrieval problem.

Because the question requires 4 independent true/false judgments to all be correct for a high score, and each rollout got at least one of statements 1, 3, or 4 wrong via the above mechanisms, no rollout scored above 3/5.
what_worked: Statement 2 (Mad Tiger / Immobilize): semantic_search on episodes correctly located the clue window (20400-20430 hit near 20460-20601), and clip_qa correctly confirmed the skill activation in 4/5 rollouts.

Rollout-4's more thorough run_sql scanning of the 30sec episodes table around the Non-Able fight let it widen its clip_qa window to 37800-38250, which was the only window across all 5 rollouts to overlap the true clue interval for statement 1, and it correctly confirmed the skill there.
Rollout-2's clip_qa on the Red Boy window correctly declined to confirm a specific 聚形散气 activation, matching the reference and avoiding the hallucination that affected the other 4 rollouts.
transferable_lessons: When a semantic_search or run_sql hit for a skill/action is a 'skill unlock/UI popup' text (e.g., 'glowing hexagonal skill emblem labeled X'), do not treat that timestamp as the usage moment -- explicitly scan forward several hundred seconds into the next combat encounter for the actual in-combat activation.

For statements referencing a generic enemy-type label (e.g., 'the Insect General') rather than a specific proper name, enumerate ALL entity rows matching that type across the entire timeline before selecting a clip_qa window, since the DB may contain several decoy entities of the same type at unrelated times and may fail to tag the actual target boss with that type at all.

Treat a clip_qa 'yes, skill visibly activated' answer with skepticism when the corresponding episodes/event_steps text for the same interval describes only generic combat/VFX and never mentions the named skill -- cross-check the visual claim against the textual description before trusting it, especially for skills defined by a distinctive visual effect (mist, cloning, immobilization) that could be confused with generic combat VFX.

For multi-statement true/false questions, verify each statement against its own clue interval independently; a single wrong-window probe or a single visual hallucination on any one statement is enough to cap the score, so window precision matters as much for 'boring' statements as for hard ones.
open_questions: Whether the boss encountered at 56816-56942 ('large, pale, armored monster... bulbous head') is in fact the 'Insect General' referenced in the question was inferred from the episodes text description only; this was not confirmed by pulling frames.

Whether the reference answer's judgment that 聚形散气 was NOT used against Red Boy (statement 4 false) is itself correct was not independently verified by pulling frames, despite 4 of 5 rollouts' visual sub-agent consistently reporting the effect; a frame check of ~75534-75582s would help adjudicate whether this is agent hallucination or a questionable reference answer.
